title: The long road to Ashford
lines: dm
The party leaves Ashford at first light and takes the north road toward Ember Gate.
a
Wren checks the map and says the road should take two days.
b
Cael ties his pack to the mule and promises to buy more rope at the first village.
dm
By noon the road runs beside a river, and a ruined mill stands on the far bank.
a
Wren sees a thin line of smoke rising from the mill chimney.
b
Cael wades across the river to look inside the mill.
dm
Inside, the mill is empty except for a fresh fire and a pot of stew still warm.
b
Cael tastes the stew and decides it is safe, and calls Wren over.
a
Wren searches the mill and finds a loose floorboard with a brass key under it.
dm
The key is stamped with a small gate and the letters EG.
a
Wren pockets the key and says the letters must mean Ember Gate.
dm
As evening falls, hoofbeats sound from the north, three riders at least.
b
Cael hides the mule behind the mill and draws his hatchet.
dm
The riders stop at the river and call out for whoever lit the fire.
a
Wren answers that the fire was theirs, and asks the riders their business.
dm
The lead rider says they ride for the gate and the gate is closed to strangers.
b
Cael asks why the gate is closed.
dm
The rider says only that the watch has been doubled since the bells stopped ringing.
a
Wren offers to share the stew if the riders will share their news of the road.
dm
The riders dismount, and the lead rider takes off her helmet to reveal a scar across her cheek.
b
Cael stays by the door with his hand on the hatchet through the whole meal.
dm
In the night, the scarred rider asks to see the brass key, and Wren says she never mentioned it.
a
Wren holds the key tightly and says she is going to sleep with it under her pillow.
dm
The scarred rider smiles and says that is a fine plan, and the fire burns low.
